newsitem.title: USA: Cooper Industries resumes repurchase plan.
newsitem.headline: Cooper Industries resumes repurchase plan.

text.p: Cooper Industries Inc said on Monday that it will resume a common stock repurchase program for up to $300 million.

Cooper directors originally authorized the plan in October 1993, a company spokesperson said. The company bought back $25 million of common stock over time, with the last sale occurring in the second quarter of 1994. Currently, $275 million of that program remains available, the company said.
Cooper intends to repurchase its stock in open market transactions, the company added.

"In light of our significantly improved debt ratio and continuing strong cash flow, we think these stock repurchases are in the best interest of our shareholders," said H. John Riley, Jr., Cooper's president and chief executive officer.
Cooper Industries is a worldwide manufacturer of electrical products, tools, hardware and automotive products.
